title: Plains, and why people live there

nodes: Rivers bring alluvium down from the mountains
Sand, silt, clay, and plant and animal matter
props.label: Plains, p.48

scenes.narration: A plain is a broad area of relatively flat land, around 200 metres above mean sea level. Rivers bring alluvium down from the mountains and deposit it, making highly fertile alluvial tracts.

nodes: Mountains: rivers begin here; bring rain; block hot and cold winds
Plateaus: minerals; waterfalls for hydro-electric power
props.label: Landforms and people, p.48

scenes.narration: Landforms shape how people live. Most rivers begin in the mountains. Plateaus have minerals, and waterfalls for hydro-electric power. Plains are the main crop growing regions.

nodes: Easier to build roads and railways
props.label: pp.48–49

scenes.narration: Because plains are fertile and flat, and it is easier to build roads and railways there, they give better conditions for living. So plains are the most densely populated regions on Earth.
